_comment: Targeted RFI review benchmark. Each case is an RFI a person really issued, used ONLY as the expected OUTPUT: the review never sees it.
A case passes when one candidate of the run matches every field of an expected finding. `pairs` are grid names or values that must appear as 'a = b' in either order;
`sheets` must each be named in the finding's evidence. Candidates matching no expected finding are listed, never scored as wrong: the sheets may carry real problems nobody wrote an RFI for.

`rejected` lists findings a person reviewed and judged WRONG, with why: a run that raises one again is a false positive and fails (the one exception to 'never scored as wrong'). Match on checkTypes, sheets in the evidence, and `mentions` in the wording. Target type 'scan' means the project-wide checks: score with --scan <rfi scan id>.
Run: python benchmarks/rfi_eval.py --run <review run id> [--case rfi-002] with DATABASE_URL set.

cases.source: BIM RFI 002 'CONFIRM THE GRID LAYOUT': 'Please confirm the correct grid layout, as a mismatch has been observed between the Architectural and Structural drawings.'

expected.what: The same grid lines are named differently on the structural and the architectural plan

cases.source: BIM RFI 015 'Discrepancies in dimensions and column location' (A3.27, A3.35): 'Please clarify the correct column locations and intended markings so the model can be updated accurately for further coordination and development.' Markup: the columns along one wall line of the Level 14 enlarged plan (A3.35, 1/4") do not sit where the Level 14 overall plan (A3.27, 1/8") shows them.
cases.knownGap: Not findable from these two sheets, and correctly so. Laid over each other by the column overlay (plan_match), A3.35 and A3.27 AGREE: detail 1 matches 4 columns and detail 2 matches 5, with no difference except a column the enlarged detail's window cuts off. The RFI's green boxes are the author's own markup (Square annotations) showing where the LEVEL BELOW puts its columns, which neither sheet carries. Comparing level 14 with level 13 is now refused by design (rfi_columns.comparable_alignments): the client rejected A3.03 (Level 4) vs A3.05 (Level 6) because columns legitimately stop and move between floors. Whether two adjacent floors' columns stack is a structural judgement the overlay cannot make, so this RFI stays a known gap.

expected.what: Column locations along the Level 14 wall line differ between the enlarged plan and the overall plan

cases.needs: A same-level comparison that shows the discrepancy; a level-13 vs level-14 overlay is refused on purpose (see knownGap).

cases.source: Client review of a draft RFI: 'Sheet A3.03 represents the Level 4 Building Plan. Sheet A3.05 represents the Level 6 Building Plan… that entire southeast wing has stepped back into an exterior low-slope roof deck… This is a false positive.'

rejected.what: Columns 'missing' from Level 6 that stop at the Level 4 setback
rejected.why: Two different floors; columns terminate below a roof deck by design. Fixed by refusing to compare sheets whose titles name different levels.

cases.source: Client review of a draft RFI: 'Sheet S1.102 is an overall building plan… at 1/8" = 1'-0". Sheet A3.36 … contains two separate enlarged details at 1/4" = 1'-0"… both drawings use identical grid numbering… The tool falsely compared Grid 4 from the enlarged callout … to Grid 1 at the bottom of the overall building plan.'

rejected.what: Grid lines 'named differently' on an overall plan and two enlarged details
rejected.why: Different scales and two viewports on one sheet; the grids agree. Fixed by comparing grids only across pages that print a common scale, and never a grid whose label appears in two places.

cases.source: Client review of a draft RFI: '"S-8" refers to … Type S-8 pan head steel screws … on A1.06, A1.08, A1.11 … S-8 is a fastener, not a door mark and does not belong in the door schedule on A1.24.'
cases.pdf: A1.06, A1.08, A1.11, A1.24 (not in this repository)

rejected.what: S8 missing from the door schedule
rejected.why: A screw type, not a door mark. Fixed twice over: a schedule must be named for the mark's family (S is not DOOR), and a mark followed by SCREWS/BOLTS/… is a product type.

cases.source: Client review of a draft RFI: 'SR-25 is a Shear Stud Rail… Note 8: SR-X DENOTES STUD RAILS. FOR STUD RAIL SCHEDULE AND DETAILS SEE SHEET S5.131… SR-25 is already fully scheduled on S5.131… The Level Schedule … is simply a table listing building floor elevations.'
cases.pdf: S2.103, S2.107, S5.131 (not in this repository)

rejected.what: SR-25 missing from the level schedule
rejected.why: A note pointing at the stud rail schedule made the forming plan count as one, and a LEVEL schedule was taken as the stud rails' schedule. Fixed: a schedule must be a heading (not 'FOR … SCHEDULE … SEE SHEET') and named for the mark's family.

cases.source: Full project-check audit on eleven of the client's sheets (S2.105, A3.01, S5.210, S0.302, S0.200, S1.101, A3.30, A3.35, A3.27, A3.32, S2.107; markups stripped). A3.27/A3.30/A3.32/A3.35 say 'REFER TO RAMP SECTIONS ON A5.14' and S2.107 points at '1/A3.31'; both sheets belong to the issued set and were simply not in the upload.
cases.pdf: the eleven sheets above (not in this repository)

rejected.what: A5.14 'referenced but not in the drawing set'
rejected.why: Not uploaded is not not-issued. With no sheet index uploaded a missing sheet cannot be told from an unuploaded one, so it is a note asking for the index, never an RFI.

rejected.what: A3.31 'referenced but not in the drawing set'
rejected.why: Same: part of the issued set, not uploaded.

cases.pdf: the client's 423-page set (not in this repository)

rejected.what: Mark F7 'missing from the concrete finish schedule'
rejected.why: F7 is grid line F.7: the identifier index strips the dot, and every quote was a grid bubble. No mark F7 is drawn on any sheet. Fixed: a dotted label is never a schedule mark.

rejected.what: Grid lines '2.3 = 2.4; 1.4 = 1.5; G.9 = H' named differently on A3.25 and S2.106
rejected.why: The structural sheets bubble one line 2.3 at one end and 2.4 at the other (1.4/1.5 likewise), so both drawings call it 2.3; and S2.106's G.9/H bubbles sit on kinked leaders 18pt off their lines. Fixed: the same name wins a two-name line, and a leader bubble is placed where its leader lands.

rejected.what: A3.34 6'-1" against A3.13 5'-10" 'between grid lines 3.7 and 3.5'
rejected.why: Measured: both sheets draw 3.7 and 3.5 5'-10" apart at their printed scales; A3.34's 6'-1" ends 2 1/2" past grid 3.5, a dimension to something else. Fixed: fullscan_run.grid_spacing_agrees.

rejected.what: A3.34 10'-1" against A3.13 10'-0" 'between grid lines 2 and 2.3'
rejected.why: Measured: both sheets draw 2 and 2.3 10'-0" apart; A3.34's 10'-1" starts 1 1/2" short of 2.3.

rejected.what: Column C-5 (S2.106) against wall tag W1-14 (A3.05) at Room 615
rejected.why: C-5 stands on grid D and A3.05 draws that column there too; the cloud is the next wall over, where W1-14 is a wall-type TAG. A label beside the box was attributed to it.

rejected.what: 'Round column' on A3.22 against 'square column' on S2.402
rejected.why: S2.402 draws the same round column; the square around it is the cap or drop panel.

rejected.what: C-13 'west face on the grid line' on A3.05 against centred on S2.106 (Unit A4A / Room 616)
rejected.why: Measured: A3.05's 22x22 fill is centred on E/4 within half an inch, S2.106's C-13 within an inch and a half. The S2.106 cloud sat on an empty patch about 10 ft from C-13. Fixed: fullscan_run.boxes_apart and column_position_agrees.

rejected.what: Round column on A3.01 against square 22 x 22 C-10.S on S2.102 near Room B5
rejected.why: Two different columns: the A3.01 cloud is the round column at B/1.4, the S2.102 cloud is C-10.S at C/2.3 (about 38 ft away). S2.102 draws C-1 (26" DIA), round, at B/1.4, and A3.01 draws a square column at C/2.3: the sheets agree at both. Fixed: fullscan_run.boxes_apart.

Same place (E/4) but two elements: A3.21A's 4'-0" square has a smaller square inside it, and S1.101 draws a larger outline (pier P-36) round its 24 x 24 C-13. The pier was compared with the column. Prompt now says a pier/pedestal/cap outline round a column is a different element; not measured by code yet.
